questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

35 × 7 ÷ 6 + 3 – 14 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66cdbc4c39141312fea1811457639ff8325fa1419d80bb0e3b665fcb681f8042.png] 

Given: 35 × 7 ÷ 6 + 3 – 14 = ?

Sign Interchange: '+' and '–', and '×' and '÷'.

After sign Interchange: 35 ÷ 7 × 6 – 3 + 14

**Apply the order of operations (BODMAS).**

→ __**35 ÷ 7**__ × 6 – 3 + 14

→ **__5__**__** × 6**__ – 3 + 14

→ 30 – 3 + 14

→ 27 + 14

**→ 41**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

16 ÷ 8 + 13 + 36 × 18 – 3 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66cdbc4c39141312fea1811457639ff8325fa1419d80bb0e3b665fcb681f8042.png] 

Given: 16 ÷ 8 + 13 + 36 × 18 – 3 = ?

Sign Interchange '+' and '–', and '×' and '÷'.

After sign interchange: 16 × 8 – 13 – 36 ÷ 18 + 3

**Apply the order of operations (BODMAS).**

→ 16 × 8 – 13 – __**36 ÷ 18**__ + 3

→ __**16 × 8**__ – 13 – 2 + 3

→ __**128**____** – 13**__ – 2 + 3

→ 115 – 2 + 3

**→ 116**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). D sits third to the left of E. questions.solution:

A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

G sits second to the left of B. Only E sits between F and G.

D sits third to the left of E. A is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Thus, 'A' sits fourth to the right of C.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
Seven friends, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). D is an immediate neighbour of both A and F. B is sitting to the immediate right of F. C is sitting second to the left of A. G and E both are C's immediate neighbours and G is not an immediate neighbour of A.

Who is the immediate neighbour of both B and D?
questions.solution:
Given:

Seven friends, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

C is sitting second to the left of A.

G and E both are C's immediate neighbours and G is not an immediate neighbour of A.

 D is an immediate neighbour of both A and F. B is sitting to the immediate right of F. . 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f03c23d958d7670a0f773bbf7fc43349db603181eee828a4a8a8dd139e766a30.png] 

Thus, 'F' is the immediate neighbour of both B and D.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some flutes are violins.

Some violins are tablas.

All tablas are sitars.

Conclusions:

(I) Some violins are sitars.

(II) Some flutes are tablas.
questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/575f26154eb8fa6b83fec470ccb333dba921f1aeb8f50aa7fd2ca5f3b2f5a322.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some violins are sitars → **True **(As, Some violins are tablas, All tablas are sitars. so, Some violins are sitars holds true)

(II) Some flutes are tablas → False (As, there is no direct relation between them)

Thus, Only conclusion (I) follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
